title: Periodic finite dynamics, quasienergy and controlled truncation

items.title: Finite-dimensional matrix exponential
items.design_state: Scaffolder-added local A-page prerequisite; complete definition or proof is authored in this batch.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ act on $\mathbb C^d$ with its standard complex inner product, and let $z\in\mathbb C$. Define the finite-dimensional matrix exponential by
$$e^{zA}:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^kA^k}{k!},\qquad A^0=I_d.$$
For the operator norm, $\|A^k\|\le\|A\|^k$, so the terms are dominated by the convergent scalar exponential series $\sum_{k\ge0}(|z|\|A\|)^k/k!$; the displayed series therefore converges absolutely in operator norm. The scalar exponential uses the convention $\exp z=\sum_{k\ge0}z^k/k!$.

items.title: Unitarity and differentiation of the finite Hermitian matrix exponential
items.design_state: Scaffolder-added local A-page prerequisite; complete definition or proof is authored in this batch.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $A=A^*$ be an endomorphism of $\mathbb C^d$ with its standard complex inner product, and let $\hbar>0$. For real $t$, define $E_A(t):=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ by the finite-dimensional matrix exponential defined on this page. Then $E_A(t)$ is unitary, $E_A(t+s)=E_A(t)E_A(s)$ for all real $s,t$, and its operator-norm derivative is
$$\frac{d}{dt}E_A(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}AE_A(t)= -\frac{i}{\hbar}E_A(t)A.$$

items.proof_route: Diagonalize a finite Hermitian matrix, reduce to scalar exponentials, and prove unitarity, the group law, and operator-norm differentiability.

items.title: Finite Floquet unitary normal form
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\hbar>0$, $\omega=2\pi/T$, and let $H:\mathbb R\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be continuous, $T$-periodic, and Hermitian at every time. Let $U(t,s)$ be the unitary propagator solving $i\hbar\,\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ and $U(s,s)=I_d$. There are an orthonormal basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ and real numbers $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_d$ such that
$$U(T,0)v_j=e^{-iT\varepsilon_j/\hbar}v_j\qquad(1\le j\le d).$$
Define the Hermitian matrix $H_Fv_j=\varepsilon_jv_j$ and the quasienergy classes $\varepsilon_j+\hbar\omega\mathbb Z$. With $P(t):=U(t,0)e^{itH_F/\hbar}$, $P(t)$ is a $T$-periodic unitary matrix and
$$U(t,0)=P(t)e^{-itH_F/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
The real representative $\varepsilon_j$ may be changed by any integer multiple of $\hbar\omega$ without changing its eigenphase; no preferred real branch is asserted.

references.title: Konrad Viebahn, Introduction to Floquet theory, lecture notes (2020)
references.locator: Section II, equations (10)-(20), period propagator, Hermitian Floquet Hamiltonian, and periodic micromotion.

items.proof_route: Use the unique unitary propagator, diagonalize the one-period unitary, choose real phase lifts, and prove the micromotion is periodic.

items.title: Finite-level truncation with bounded coupling error
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $\hbar>0$, let $H=H^*$ on $\mathbb C^d$, and let $P=P^*=P^2$ be an orthogonal projection. Use the operator norm induced by the standard inner product. Put $P^\perp=I_d-P$, $H_D=PHP+P^\perp HP^\perp$, and $V=H-H_D$. With finite matrix exponentials as defined on this page, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\left\|e^{-itH/\hbar}-e^{-itH_D/\hbar}\right\|\le\frac{|t|}{\hbar}\|V\|,\qquad \left\|P^\perp e^{-itH/\hbar}P\right\|\le\frac{|t|}{\hbar}\|V\|.$$
The second inequality bounds amplitude leakage from the retained subspace $\operatorname{ran}P$; it asserts no convergence for an unbounded coupling.

references.title: Konrad Viebahn, Introduction to Floquet theory, lecture notes (2020)
references.locator: Section II, equations (10)-(20), finite-dimensional unitary propagation and exact Floquet factorization; the bounded Duhamel estimate is proved locally.

items.proof_route: Differentiate the two-propagator product, integrate the bounded coupling in operator norm, and project away the block-diagonal evolution.

items.title: Finite-level Sambe operator with Fourier domain
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\omega=2\pi/T$, $\hbar>0$, and let $H:\mathbb R\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be $C^1$, $T$-periodic, and Hermitian at every time. On $\mathscr H_T=L^2((0,T),dt;\mathbb C^d)$ define
$$D(K)=\{f=(f_1,\ldots,f_d): f_a\in H^1(0,T)\text{ for every }a,\ f(0)=f(T)\},\qquad (Kf)(t)=H(t)f(t)-i\hbar f'(t).$$
Here each $H^1(0,T)$ function is represented by its unique absolutely continuous representative, so endpoint values are its traces, and $f'$ is its componentwise weak derivative. Then $K$ is self-adjoint on exactly $D(K)$. Choose $v_j$ and $\varepsilon_j$ from [[thm-nrqmx-finite-floquet-normal-form]], so $H_Fv_j=\varepsilon_jv_j$ and $P(t)$ is its periodic unitary. The functions
$$\phi_{jn}(t)=T^{-1/2}e^{in\omega t}P(t)v_j\qquad(1\le j\le d,\ n\in\mathbb Z)$$
form an orthonormal basis of $\mathscr H_T$ and satisfy $K\phi_{jn}=(\varepsilon_j+n\hbar\omega)\phi_{jn}$.

references.title: Konrad Viebahn, Introduction to Floquet theory, lecture notes (2020)
references.locator: Section IV, equations (55)-(60), periodic modes and the infinite Fourier-sector matrix; the local proof supplies the exact periodic H1 domain and self-adjointness.

references.title: André Eckardt and Egidijus Anisimovas, High-frequency approximation for periodically driven quantum systems from a Floquet-space perspective, New Journal of Physics 17 (2015), 093039
references.locator: Section 2.3, equations (17)-(20) and Appendix B, equations (184)-(185), quasienergy operator and Fourier blocks; the local proof supplies the exact domain and self-adjointness.

items.proof_route: Realize the periodic derivative on its exact H1 domain, use Kato–Rellich for self-adjointness, then use Fourier modes and the periodic micromotion to obtain the eigenbasis.

items.title: Floquet Fourier–Galerkin assembly
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $b,N\ge0$, and real numbers $\hbar>0$, $\omega>0$, and $\tau>0$. Let $H_k\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ for $-b\le k\le b$ satisfy $H_{-k}=H_k^*$; set $H_k=0$ when $|k|>b$. Thus $H(t)=\sum_{k=-b}^{b}H_ke^{ik\omega t}$ is a finite Fourier polynomial with period $T=2\pi/\omega$. Let $S_\tau$ be a caller-supplied total classical routine for finite Hermitian matrices whose declared interface returns $(2N+1)d$ real approximate eigenvalues $\widetilde\lambda_j$, an orthonormal basis $x_j$, and residuals $r_j=\|K_Nx_j-\widetilde\lambda_jx_j\|$ with target $r_j\le\tau$. This algorithm returns that finite record unchanged and does not certify its residual claims.

The algorithm takes $(d,b,N,\hbar,\omega,(H_k)_{|k|\le b},\tau,S_\tau)$ and returns a matrix $K_N$ and the eigensolver's output record:

1. Order the Fourier indices as $-N,-N+1,\ldots,N$ and allocate a $(2N+1)d$ by $(2N+1)d$ block matrix.

2. For each ordered pair $n,m\in\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, assign the $d$ by $d$ block
$$ (K_N)_{nm}:=H_{n-m}+n\hbar\omega\,\delta_{nm}I_d,$$
where $\delta_{nm}=1$ if $n=m$ and $0$ otherwise.

3. Call $S_\tau(K_N)$ once and return $(K_N,S_\tau(K_N))$.

The block assembly always terminates after $(2N+1)^2$ block assignments; the complete procedure terminates by the assumed totality of $S_\tau$. This procedure defines the exact finite compression matrix; the solver's residual claims and convergence of finite-section quasienergies are separate claims.

items.title: Fourier–Galerkin assembly correctness and termination
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $b,N\ge0$, $\hbar>0$, $\omega>0$, and $T=2\pi/\omega$. Let $H_k\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ for $|k|\le b$ satisfy $H_{-k}=H_k^*$, set $H_k=0$ for $|k|>b$, and put $H(t)=\sum_{|k|\le b}H_ke^{ik\omega t}$. Let $\mathscr H_T=L^2((0,T),dt;\mathbb C^d)$ with its componentwise $L^2$ inner product, and let $Kf=H(t)f-i\hbar f'(t)$ on the domain of vectors whose components lie in $H^1(0,T)$ and have equal endpoint traces. Let $\mathcal S_N$ be the span of $T^{-1/2}e^{in\omega t}v$ with $-N\le n\le N$ and $v\in\mathbb C^d$, and let $\Pi_N$ be its orthogonal projection. The matrix with blocks $(K_N)_{nm}=H_{n-m}+n\hbar\omega\delta_{nm}I_d$ is exactly the matrix of $\Pi_NK|_{\mathcal S_N}$ in the ordered Fourier basis. It is Hermitian. Its block construction terminates after $(2N+1)^2$ assignments; this compression identity gives no convergence or spectral-accuracy guarantee for finite-section eigenvalues.

references.locator: Section IV, equations (57)-(60), exact Fourier-sector matrix and finite truncation discussion.

items.proof_route: Compute each Fourier matrix coefficient of multiplication and derivative, use Hermitian symmetry, and count finite assignments.

items.title: Commuting longitudinal drive
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On $\mathbb C^2$ let $\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, choose real $E_0,A$, and choose $\hbar>0$, $\omega>0$, and $T=2\pi/\omega$. For $H(t)=(E_0+A\cos(\omega t))\sigma_z$, the unique propagator from time $0$ is
$$U(t,0)=\exp\!\left[-\frac{i}{\hbar}\left(E_0t+\frac{A}{\omega}\sin(\omega t)\right)\sigma_z\right].$$
One Floquet normal form is $H_F=E_0\sigma_z$ and $P(t)=\exp[-iA\sin(\omega t)\sigma_z/(\hbar\omega)]$.
